implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control (P06) was approved 2026-08-31. Account management procedures for the ATS, payroll platform, and E-Verify are due 2026-11-30.

Internal staff accounts are created in the identity provider from HR onboarding tickets and federated to the ATS, cloud console, and timekeeping admin portal. Associate self-service accounts are created by the ATS at onboarding. Gap: the payroll platform and E-Verify accounts are managed by hand outside SSO, there is no quarterly access review, and 2 E-Verify accounts of departed staff were active at P07 testing.
evidence: IdP user export; E-Verify user list; termination tickets
regulatory_driver: N56-BM (PR.AA-01); E-Verify MOU Art. II.A.3; N56-R03 (8 CFR 274a.2(g)(1)(i))

implementation_statement: The ATS enforces roles (recruiter, account manager, onboarding, payroll, admin) and branch assignment. Gap: the recruiter role can open I-9 document images and consumer report PDFs for all 4 branches.

The Controller approves each weekly payroll register before funding. Gap: Payroll Specialists can both change associate bank accounts and submit the payroll that pays them, with no second review of bank changes.
Staff do not have local admin rights on laptops. Gap: all 22 recruiters can query the reporting database, which holds full SSNs and bank account numbers; 2 cloud administrators hold standing rights.
The identity provider locks accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts. The payroll platform locks after 5 failed attempts.
Laptops lock after 10 minutes idle through device management. Gap: lobby kiosks run under a shared local account with no session reset between applicants.
The ATS ends idle sessions after 30 minutes and the payroll platform after 20 minutes (vendor settings confirmed).
There is no VPN into the offices. Staff reach SaaS systems over TLS through SSO. The managed IT provider uses a remote support tool with named accounts and MFA, limited to IT-approved sessions.
The 34 company smartphones are enrolled in device management with passcode, encryption, and remote wipe.
The awareness and training policy is included in POL-05 (P06). Training procedures are due 2026-11-30.
Internal staff watch an annual security video. Gap: no phishing exercises, no reminders, and nothing on payroll diversion or invoice fraud.

Every E-Verify user completed the E-Verify Tutorial before creating cases (MOU Art. II.A.5). Gap: no role training for payroll staff on bank-change fraud, or for recruiters on FCRA and I-9 record handling.
regulatory_driver: E-Verify MOU Art. II.A.5; N56-R03 (8 CFR 274a.2(g)(1)(iii))

implementation_statement: The ATS, payroll platform, identity provider, and cloud tenant log sign-ins and admin actions by default. Gap: object-level access logging is off on the document archive, and the firm has not defined which events it needs.
ATS and payroll audit records include user, record, field, old and new value, date and time, and source address. The I-9 module keeps a change history per form.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: no one reviews audit logs. Planned: weekly review of payroll exports, bank-account changes, ATS admin actions, and identity provider risky sign-ins, starting 2026-10.
The ATS and payroll platform keep audit history for the life of the record. Gap: identity provider logs are kept 30 days and cloud logs 90 days.
Audit record generation is on by default in the SaaS systems and the cloud control plane. Gap: data access events for the object storage archive and the reporting database are not generated.
An independent control assessment was performed 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-07 (P07).
Planned: quarterly review of the POA&M, key metrics, and AI tool monitoring results by the COO.
A standard laptop image exists. Gap: no documented baseline for kiosks, branch firewalls, or the cloud workloads.

Gap: no change control for ATS workflow settings, the integration service, or AI tool settings. The AI tool's auto-advance mode was switched on in 2026-03 without review. Planned: change log with COO approval for high-impact settings.
Laptop settings are enforced through device management. Gap: cloud workload hardening and kiosk lockdown are not documented.
Unneeded services are disabled on the laptop image. Gap: kiosks allow general web browsing and USB storage.
Laptops and phones are inventoried in device management. Gap: kiosks, scanners, network gear, and data stores (where SSNs and I-9 images are kept) are not inventoried.
Contingency planning policy due 2026-12-31.
Gap: no contingency plan, manual payroll procedure, or ATS downtime procedure. The BIA (P05) was approved 2026-08-31 to inform the plan due 2026-12-31.
Gap: no restore test has ever been performed. First restore test of the reporting database and I-9 archive scheduled 2026-10-15.

implementation_statement: ATS and payroll data are backed up by the vendors. The reporting database and document archive are snapshotted daily. Gap: snapshots share the production account, region, and administrators and are not immutable.
Recovery procedures will be documented in the contingency plan due 2026-12-31.

Staff authenticate with unique IDs through the identity provider for SSO systems. Gap: the payroll platform and E-Verify use separate local accounts, and a departed colleague's E-Verify login was used by another person (P07).
evidence: IdP user export; E-Verify user list

implementation_statement: Number-matching push MFA is required for administrators of the identity provider, ATS, and cloud console. Gap: payroll platform administrators use SMS codes.
All SSO users have push MFA. Gap: payroll platform users (including 6 payroll and billing staff) use SMS codes that can be relayed by a phishing proxy (R-001).
The identity provider enforces a 14-character minimum and a banned-password list. Gap: kiosks share one local password, and E-Verify passwords were shared.

New associates' identity is proofed at hire through Form I-9 document examination (in person at branches, or the DHS remote alternative procedure for Office and Administrative hires) and E-Verify, before an associate portal account is issued. Gap: no written checklist for the remote live video examination.
POL-03 Incident Response Policy was approved 2026-08-31 (P06).
Incidents are handled ad hoc by the IT Manager and the managed IT provider. The payroll breach runbook (P08) was approved 2026-08-31; the tabletop is due 2026-11-30.
Planned: security incident category in the IT ticketing system.
Notice duties (Florida, other states, E-Verify MOU, clients) are defined in the P08 notification matrix. Gap: staff have not been told how to report suspected incidents.
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(3); (4); E-Verify MOU Art. II.A.16

implementation_statement: Incident response plan elements are documented in POL-03 and the P08 runbook.
Paper with SSNs, I-9 copies, and consumer reports goes to locked shred bins; the vendor issues certificates. Gap: laptop wipes are not recorded and a kiosk PC was discarded unwiped in 2025.
HQ uses badge access with a maintained list. Gap: Branches 2-4 use keyed locks and no key log.
Network closets are locked at all offices; paper onboarding files are kept in locked cabinets. Gap: the Branch 3 closet also stores lobby supplies and is often left open during business hours.

implementation_statement: The career site has an applicant privacy notice. Gap: the FCRA disclosure is not a standalone document, and candidates are not told that an AI tool ranks applications.
Risk assessment policy is in POL-01 section 4.
The APATP is categorized Moderate (section 6 of this SSP).
Risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 using NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). Annual update scheduled.
The managed IT provider scans the 4 office firewalls from the internet quarterly. Gap: no internal, kiosk, or cloud workload scanning.
Risk responses are recorded in the P01 register and tracked in the P07 POA&M.
Critical processes and components are identified in the BIA (P05).
The payroll vendor contract has security and breach notice terms. Gap: no standard security terms for new vendors; the AI vendor was bought through the ATS marketplace with click-through terms.
The payroll vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report is on file (reviewed in P09 Part B). Gap: no SOC 2 or questionnaire for the ATS, AI, timekeeping, or screening vendors.

Office firewalls block inbound traffic; guest Wi-Fi is separate from staff Wi-Fi. The reporting database accepts connections only from the integration service and office addresses. Gap: lobby kiosks sit on the staff network.
TLS 1.2 or higher for all SaaS, the career site, and the integration service APIs. Payroll files to the vendor's bank travel within the vendor's platform.
Providers use validated cryptographic modules per their SOC 2 system descriptions and service documentation.
ATS, payroll, database, and object storage data are encrypted at rest by the providers; laptops use full-disk encryption.
Laptop OS and browser patches install automatically. Gap: the integration service container image and kiosks are not patched on a schedule.
EDR on all laptops. Gap: kiosks run built-in antivirus only.
The managed IT provider reviews EDR alerts the next business day. Gap: no after-hours response and no alerting on SaaS events (payroll exports, bank changes).

Forms I-9 are kept in the ATS and archive. Gap: no retention schedule: I-9s, document images, and consumer reports are kept indefinitely instead of being purged after the retention period (3 years after hire or 1 year after termination, whichever is later, for I-9s).
